title: Generative AI should support learning goals
claim: Generative AI can support learning when its use is guided by clear teaching principles; completing a task successfully does not necessarily mean that learning has improved.
evidence: The OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026 discusses the conditions for effective use of generative AI in education, including pedagogical guidance, learning objectives, privacy, safety, transparency and age-appropriateness.
strategic_implication: Evaluate AI-assisted grading, tutoring and learning support against educational outcomes and teacher-reviewed quality, not just task completion or automation volume.

title: Protect learner privacy when adopting generative AI
claim: Educational adoption of generative AI requires safeguards for data privacy and a human-centred approach appropriate to learners' ages and needs.
evidence: UNESCO's guidance on generative AI in education and research discusses data privacy, age-appropriate use, human agency, inclusion, equity and the need to validate educational tools.
strategic_implication: Establish rules for student-data handling, age-appropriate access, human oversight and review of AI tools before expanding AI-enabled educational services.

title: Keep educators involved in AI-enabled teaching
source_name: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Educational Technology
claim: AI adoption in education should be designed around teaching and learning needs, with attention to human involvement and the risks of automated systems.
evidence: The U.S. Department of Education's 2023 report examines opportunities and risks associated with AI in teaching and learning and provides recommendations for educational technology design and implementation.
strategic_implication: Design grading and student-support workflows so that educators can review consequential AI outputs, correct errors and retain responsibility for important educational decisions.

title: Build a coherent and governed digital education ecosystem
claim: Digital education transformation depends on how educational systems, data, tools and governance work together, including attention to privacy, equity and interoperability.
evidence: The OECD Digital Education Outlook 2023 examines education management information systems, learning management systems, digital assessment platforms and the governance of education data and technology.
strategic_implication: Assess integration between the LMS, student information systems and assessment tools; define data ownership, access controls, interoperability requirements and privacy safeguards before building new analytics.
